extracted.intended_audience: researchers and students in cognitive psychology, cognitive science, and humor research
extracted.subtask_description: Theoretical and empirical analysis of the cognitive mechanisms (e.g., incongruity-resolution, two-stage processing, developmental factors) that underlie comprehension and appreciation of jokes, cartoons, and other humorous stimuli.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on cognitive (not just affective) aspects
rubrics_metrics.description: When we think about humorous experience our attention is typically focused on its affective or emotional aspects... The affect surrounding humor may make us overlook the cognitive effort that is essential for its comprehension and appreciation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers and analysts should explicitly examine cognitive processes (comprehension, resolution, mental operations) in addition to emotional responses when studying or evaluating humor. Avoid treating humor solely as an affective phenomenon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge cognitive effort essential for comprehension and appreciation
rubrics_metrics.description: The cognitive effort that is essential for its comprehension and appreciation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretations of humor should account for underlying mental operations required to decode meaning and resolve incongruities; measurement and experimental designs should probe cognitive demands (e.g., processing time, problem-solving components).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize that effective humor appears instantaneous despite complex processing
rubrics_metrics.description: When humor is most effective, the mental work occurs instantaneously and apparently without effort. But producing and understanding one’s native language are no less phenomenologically instantaneous and effortless. Nonetheless, there is substantial evidence ... that complex mental processes are at work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not equate phenomenological ease with lack of processing complexity. Use reaction-time, developmental, and linguistic analyses to reveal hidden cognitive steps even when appreciation seems immediate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground accounts of humor in linguistics and cognitive psychology evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: There is substantial evidence from the fields of linguistics and cognitive psychology that complex mental processes are at work (Fodor, Bever, & Garrett, 1974; Chomsky, 1965).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anchor theoretical claims and empirical studies in relevant linguistic and cognitive frameworks (e.g., syntax/semantics, language processing models). Cite and build on established work from those fields when explaining humor comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider incongruity-resolution and tension/arousal theories
rubrics_metrics.description: References to 'Incongruity versus tension relief: Hypotheses of humor' and studies on 'incongruity and resolution' appear repeatedly in the literature cited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating or constructing humor theories or stimuli, explicitly test how incongruity is presented and resolved and how arousal/tension-relief mechanisms contribute to amusement; use experimental paradigms that manipulate expectancy violation and resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ stage or process models (e.g., Suls' two-stage model)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suls: 'A two-stage model for the appreciation of jokes and cartoons.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multi-stage frameworks (e.g., initial detection of anomaly followed by resolution/evaluation) to analyze humor comprehension and design experiments that can separate stages (detection, resolution, affective response).

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for developmental and individual-difference factors in humor appreciation
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple cited works address children's comprehension (McGhee, Shultz) and individual differences (Leventhal, Cupchik, Rothbart).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how age, cognitive development, operational thinking, personality, and reference-group identification influence humor comprehension and preference; tailor methods and interpretations to developmental stage and individual differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include affective/disparagement dimensions alongside cognitive analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: References to 'Cognitive and disparagement theories of humour' and studies on 'Disparagement humor: Dispositions and resolutions.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate affective, social, and moral dimensions (e.g., disparagement, audience identification) with cognitive-process accounts to explain when humor elicits amusement versus offense; design studies to measure both cognitive resolution and affective reactions.
